svg.title: Graphical rendering of the RIAA transformation
svg.desc: Equal-level 50 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz tones before recording EQ, after recording EQ as cut into the groove, and after complementary playback EQ. A lower panel shows groove displacement versus frequency with and without RIAA.
svg.text: Each row is the same tone at three stages. Wave height is linear voltage, to scale. Cycle density follows frequency.
Equal voltage — this is the musical balance
The phono stage restores the original
What that does to the groove
The cutter is a constant-velocity transducer, so displacement falls as 1/f. Recording EQ is applied on top of that. Values relative to 1 kHz = 1×.
electrical curve, so the listener hears
